reports.author: Claude
reports.title: Speech-engine benchmark: which AI hears Medi's Arabic
reports.question: On the 63 moments Medi corrected in the 10-02 transcript, which speech engine writes the word he actually said, without hiding his mistakes?
reports.verdict: Gemini 3.8 Flash, listening to his microphone with the lesson around it, heard 53 of 63. Today's engine (ElevenLabs) heard 4 and no plain transcriber passed 21. On 2026-10-04 twelve ideas were tried on top of it, one at a time (evidence labels, word confidence, a second guess, an accent note, the lesson's word list, vowel marks, more thinking, a one-field answer): none beat 53 beyond the run-to-run noise, and the combined best recipe scored 49. Flash still changes a word on about 60 lines he left alone, so its changes are proposals, not automatic. All of it was measured on one lesson.

reports.title: Engineering audit: do all the numbers add up?
reports.question: Is everything engineered correctly: do the formulas add up across every page, and are the reports right?
reports.verdict: They did not. The same slip was counted twice, two pages used two grammar formulas, and nothing checked the math before going live. All of that is fixed on a branch, and a guard now checks every hour. Every score shows ≈ until a person verifies it.

reports.author: Claude
reports.title: Engineering review: measure every AI step before adding more
reports.question: From a pure engineering and AI point of view, how should Anees be built and tracked, and what do the research on transcription, learner comprehension, dialect translation and Levantine ASR say it should change?
reports.verdict: The big bets hold: Scribe v2, separate tracks, FSRS, and Amal's own Arabizi spelling. The weak spot is measurement: 1 of 9 AI steps has a gold set, 0 AI calls are logged, and the free-form Claude readers are the step most likely to be wrong on dialect (LLMs score 53.8 vs 88.9 on dialect grammar). Build order: run log, decisions log, frozen gold sets, health panel.

reports.author: Claude
reports.title: Process review: the AI gets measured once, then trusted
reports.question: How is each AI step from recording to pages checked today, what data is lost, and what should be tracked?
reports.verdict: The grammar detector scores 76% on the rows it was tuned on and 11% on real lessons. The two AI readers agree on 61.5% of rows (target 95%). No run records model, cost or time. 18 rules wait for Medi's yes/no and 116 items wait on Amal.

reports.author: Claude
reports.title: Listening research: which sentence tags predict what Medi understands
reports.question: Beyond length, tense and endings, what does research say makes a spoken sentence hard for an L2 listener, and which planned tags does the evidence support?
reports.verdict: Tag the unknown key word first: a rare word merely present barely matters, a rare word needed for the meaning is one of the strongest effects. Then audio trouble, pause structure, repeat count and words known by ear. Tense, endings and noun share have no listening studies: they are Anees's own hypotheses to test. A bare 'aywa' counts as unknown, not understood.

reports.author: Claude
reports.title: Process audit: why the detector missed 857 of 961 slips
reports.question: The hand audit found 961 slips across 13 lessons. Why did the grammar detector catch only 104, and what rule stops each kind of miss?
reports.verdict: The machine caught 104 of 961 rows (11%). 15 gaps explain the 857 misses; a 16th (wrong bucket) spoils a third of the hits. 18 rules close them, one at a time, for Medi's yes/no. Amal has to touch 7 of the 66 B patterns.

reports.title: Adversarial audit of the Codex bake-off and the project
reports.question: Does Codex's 'keep ElevenLabs' survive a recount from raw JSON, audio measurement and a repo read?
reports.verdict: Yes, on the full lesson track only. On 25-second chunks the same engine lost 3 of 8 of Medi's mistakes. Clip 16, not 14, is the cleanest vocabulary-poisoning case. The report email could go out before the page was pushed (fixed today).

reports.author: Codex
reports.title: Overnight bake-off: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe and CrisperWhisper 2.0
reports.question: Can Gemini, xAI, Inworld, Fish, StepAudio, Cartesia or a local model beat ElevenLabs on the same 20 frozen clips?
reports.verdict: No. Gemini's best arm found 14 of 20 target families but inserted a word the audio did not support. CrisperWhisper kept fillers but lost most targets and looped on 4 of 40 clips. xAI is the best untested option.

reports.author: Codex
reports.title: Fish Audio: research and test status
reports.question: Is Fish Audio's cheap ASR worth Amal's audio?
reports.verdict: Not now. Its API has no vocabulary, verbatim, speaker or word-timing controls, its terms allow training on uploads, and it costs more than ElevenLabs. Test only with Amal's informed consent.
reports.bars_title: Verbatim benchmark, English, filler F1 (Nyra Labs; interested party)

reports.author: Codex
reports.title: Full deep research: capture, engines, architecture, project audit
reports.question: What should Anees be built around, and does anything beat ElevenLabs?
reports.verdict: Build a better system around ElevenLabs, not a better engine: Ennuicastr separate tracks on Android, Scribe per track without keyterms, a 20-item Amal inbox. Speechmatics Melia tested and rejected as primary. Six P0 findings in the repo.

reports.author: Codex
reports.title: Independent test: ElevenLabs vs OpenAI on 20 frozen clips
reports.question: Does a strict OpenAI prompt beat ElevenLabs at keeping Medi's words?
reports.verdict: No. The strict prompt fixed OpenAI's wrong-language habit but removed every filler and found fewer target families. Adding the vocabulary list to the prompt made it worse.

reports.author: Claude
reports.title: Engine report: 14 engines on the Aug 25 lesson
reports.question: Which transcriber should Anees use for now?
reports.verdict: ElevenLabs Scribe v2 for now: Amal preferred it on 15 of 20 blind clips against Speechmatics and a local Whisper (OpenAI was not in that vote). It wins on words and hesitations kept, not on a human accuracy score.
